methods.label: Use the intercept-form restriction
methods.explanation: Intercept form requires both intercepts to be nonzero. For a line through the origin, at least one intercept is 0.
methods.levelReason: This applies the defining nonzero-intercept condition within the stated elective scope.

methods.label: Substitute the origin
methods.explanation: For \(x/a+y/b=1\) to be defined, \(a\ne0\) and \(b\ne0\). A line through the origin must contain \((0,0)\), but substituting these coordinates gives \(0/a+0/b=0\), whereas the equation requires the left side to equal \(1\). Thus no line through the origin has this intercept form. The answer is B.
methods.levelReason: Testing whether a coordinate pair satisfies an equation uses only elementary algebra and coordinates.
